experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the largest ancient castle complex in the world, including St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Walk the cobblestone streets of Hradčany district and enjoy panoramic views over the red-roofed city. A guided tour brings centuries of Bohemian history to life.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in one of Europe's largest and most iconic thermal bath complexes, built in 1913 in stunning Neo-Baroque style. The geothermal waters have been used since Roman times, making this a deeply historical and rejuvenating cultural experience unique to Budapest.

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Walking Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the medieval Old Town Square, witness the hourly show of the 15th-century Astronomical Clock (Orloj), and explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) with its hauntingly preserved synagogues and cemetery. A self-guided or budget group tour covers centuries of layered history.

experiences.name: Budapest Danube River Evening Cruise
experiences.description: Sail along the Danube at dusk and witness the illuminated Hungarian Parliament Building, Buda Castle, and Chain Bridge — a UNESCO World Heritage riverside panorama. This iconic cruise offers a breathtaking perspective on Budapest's architectural grandeur and imperial history.

experiences.name: Prague to Budapest Scenic Train Journey & Local Food Tasting
experiences.description: Travel between Prague and Budapest by scenic overnight or daytime train, embracing the city-hopping spirit of Central Europe. Upon arrival in Budapest, explore the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) for traditional Hungarian street food including lángos, chimney cake, and goulash soup.
experiences.location: Praha Hlavní Nádraží to Keleti Station, Budapest

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Václav Havel Airport Prague at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Airport Express bus (Line AE) to Náměstí Republiky for ~60 CZK (~$2.50 USD). Check in to your hostel/budget accommodation in Prague Old Town area. Grab a late-night snack from a 24-hour convenience store or nearby kebab stand near Wenceslas Square.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Late-night street food near Wenceslas Square – try a trdelník or kebab for under 100 CZK (~$4)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – only arrival tasks. Buy a 24-hour Prague public transport pass (120 CZK) at the airport for the next day. Exchange a small amount of cash to Czech Koruna (CZK) at the airport or use a no-fee card.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a free self-guided walk through Prague Old Town (Staré Město). Visit the iconic Old Town Square, watch the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime at the top of the hour (free to watch from outside). Explore the narrow cobblestone lanes and admire Gothic and Baroque architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the famous Charles Bridge (free) for stunning views of the Vltava River and Prague Castle. Climb up to Prague Castle complex – entry to the castle grounds is free; pay only for specific interiors (St. Vitus Cathedral interior ~250 CZK). Wander the Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička) for a glimpse into medieval life.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood for a relaxed evening stroll. Visit Kampa Island and the John Lennon Wall (free). Enjoy dinner at a local Czech pub in Malá Strana.

meals.breakfast: Budget hostel breakfast or grab a fresh pastry (rohlík) and coffee from a local bakery for ~50 CZK
meals.lunch: Street food near Charles Bridge – try a svíčková sandwich or sausage from a market stall for ~80–120 CZK
meals.dinner: Traditional Czech pub (hospoda) – order svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings + local Pilsner Urquell beer for ~200–300 CZK total

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – Prague Old Town is almost entirely walkable. Avoid tourist-trap restaurants directly on Old Town Square; walk one block away for much better prices.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Vyšehrad fortress (free entry to grounds) – a hidden gem with panoramic views over Prague and the Vltava River. Explore the ancient Romanesque rotunda, the Vyšehrad Cemetery (famous Czechs buried here), and the twin-spired Basilica of St. Peter and Paul (small entry fee ~50 CZK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take tram #17 along the river to Holešovice neighborhood and visit the DOX Centre for Contemporary Art or explore the Letná Park (free) with its famous giant metronome and sweeping views of Prague's rooftops. Alternatively, visit the free Municipal House (Obecní dům) lobby and admire Art Nouveau architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the hip Žižkov neighborhood – known for the quirky Žižkov Television Tower with crawling baby sculptures (free to view outside). Browse local bars and enjoy a cheap Czech beer (prices start at ~30–50 CZK per pint in local pubs away from tourist zones).

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre-style budget alternative – find a local kavárna (café) for coffee and toast for ~80 CZK
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh open-faced sandwich (chlebíčky) from a local deli (lahůdky) for ~30–50 CZK each
meals.dinner: Žižkov local pub dinner – try fried cheese (smažený sýr) with tartar sauce or roast pork knee (vepřové koleno) for ~150–250 CZK

day_by_day.notes: September weather in Prague is mild (15–20°C / 59–68°F) – bring a light jacket for evenings. The Žižkov area is very local and budget-friendly compared to Old Town.

day_by_day.morning: Morning free time to revisit any Prague highlights or explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) – walk the exterior for free; synagogue entries require a ticket (~350 CZK for combined ticket). Visit the historic Jewish Cemetery if budget allows. Pack your bags and prepare for the journey to Budapest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the budget RegioJet or FlixBus from Prague to Budapest (journey ~7 hours, tickets from €10–20 booked in advance). Buses depart from Florenc Bus Station, easily reachable by metro. Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside en route. Arrive in Budapest early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to your Budapest budget accommodation (hostel in District VII – Jewish Quarter area recommended). Take a short orientation walk around the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (exterior free at night) and explore the ruin bars of the Jewish Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick pastry and coffee at Prague's Florenc bus station or a nearby bakery for ~60–80 CZK
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for the bus – buy fresh bread, cheese, and cold cuts from a Prague supermarket (Albert or Billa) for ~100 CZK
meals.dinner: Arrive in Budapest and eat at a lángos stand (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) near the Jewish Quarter for ~800–1,200 HUF (~$2–3 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book RegioJet or FlixBus tickets at least 1–2 weeks in advance for the best prices. The bus is more budget-friendly than the train. Keep your passport handy as you cross the Czech-Slovak-Hungarian borders.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Budapest's Castle District (Várhegy) on the Buda side. Take the funicular (Sikló) up Castle Hill (~1,400 HUF one way) or walk up for free. Visit Buda Castle (exterior free), Matthias Church (entry ~2,500 HUF), and the Fisherman's Bastion (free access to terraces, premium areas ~1,000 HUF) with spectacular views over the Danube and Pest side.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down through Castle Hill and cross the iconic Széchenyi Chain Bridge (free pedestrian access) to the Pest side. Stroll along the Danube Promenade and visit the haunting Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial (free). Head to the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) – browse fresh produce, Hungarian paprika, and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the famous ruin bars of District VII – start with Szimpla Kert, the original ruin bar (free entry most evenings). Enjoy cheap local craft beers or pálinka (Hungarian brandy). The neighborhood comes alive on weekend evenings.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or a Hungarian langos or fresh bread roll from a local pékség (bakery) for ~500–800 HUF
meals.lunch: Grab a meal at the Great Market Hall's upper floor food stalls – try goulash soup or stuffed cabbage for ~1,500–2,000 HUF
meals.dinner: Ruin bar area street food or a nearby étterem (restaurant) – try lángos, kürtőskalács (chimney cake), or a hearty Hungarian stew for ~2,000–3,000 HUF

day_by_day.notes: Budapest uses Hungarian Forint (HUF). As of 2027, budget ~3,500–5,000 HUF/day for meals. Use Budapest's excellent metro/tram system – a 24-hour pass costs ~2,500 HUF and covers all public transport.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) – one of Europe's most stunning neo-Gothic buildings. English guided tours are available (~8,000 HUF for non-EU visitors). Admire the exterior from the Danube bank for free. Explore Liberty Square (Szabadság tér) and its monuments nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) – completely free and one of Budapest's most iconic landmarks. Walk through City Park (Városliget) and see the exterior of Vajdahunyad Castle (park entry free, castle museum ~2,000 HUF). On Sundays, there's often a local market in the park.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a budget-friendly thermal bath experience at Széchenyi Baths in City Park (~6,500–8,000 HUF for evening entry – cheaper than daytime). Soak in the outdoor pools as the September evening cools down. A quintessential Budapest experience.

meals.breakfast: Local Hungarian breakfast at a cukrászda (pastry shop) – try rétes (strudel) with coffee for ~1,000–1,500 HUF
meals.lunch: City Park area – bring a picnic from a local supermarket (Spar or Aldi) for ~1,000–1,500 HUF, or eat at a nearby étterem
meals.dinner: Post-bath dinner at a simple Hungarian restaurant near City Park or back in District VII – try chicken paprikash with nokedli (egg noodles) for ~2,500–3,500 HUF

day_by_day.notes: Book Széchenyi Baths online in advance to secure your preferred time slot and potentially save on entry fees. Bring flip-flops and a towel (or rent one at the baths for ~1,000 HUF). Sunday is a great day for the baths as the atmosphere is lively.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) – the largest synagogue in Europe (~5,000 HUF entry includes museum and memorial garden). Explore the Hungarian Jewish Museum and the poignant Raoul Wallenberg Memorial Park. A deeply moving cultural and historical experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Pest side on foot – walk down Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's Champs-Élysées, free to stroll) and visit the Hungarian State Opera House exterior (tours available ~4,500 HUF if budget allows). Browse the eclectic shops and cafés along the way. Visit the atmospheric Kerepesi Cemetery (free) – final resting place of Hungarian national heroes.
day_by_day.evening: Take tram #2 along the Danube for one of Budapest's most scenic and free rides, offering beautiful views of the illuminated Buda Castle and Chain Bridge at dusk. End the evening with a sunset walk across Margaret Bridge to Margaret Island (Margit-sziget) – a peaceful green oasis in the middle of the Danube (free entry).

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud-style alternative – find a local cukrászda for coffee and a slice of Dobos torte (Hungarian layer cake) for ~1,500 HUF
meals.lunch: Andrássy Avenue area – try a local lunchtime étterem offering a napi menü (daily set menu: soup + main course) for ~2,000–3,000 HUF – excellent value
meals.dinner: Margaret Island or riverside – pack a picnic or grab street food; alternatively dine at a budget restaurant in District VI or VII for ~2,000–3,000 HUF

day_by_day.notes: The napi menü (daily lunch menu) is the best budget dining hack in Budapest – available Monday–Friday at most restaurants between 12:00–15:00, offering 2–3 courses for a fraction of the à la carte price.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest – revisit a favorite spot or explore the Citadella fortress on Gellért Hill (free to hike up, ~30–40 min walk) for the best panoramic views of the entire city. See the Liberty Statue (Szabadság-szobor) and take in sweeping views of both Buda and Pest sides of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Great Market Hall or local shops – pick up Hungarian paprika, pálinka, or embroidered folk crafts as budget-friendly gifts. Head to Budapest Keleti or Kelenföldi station for onward transport, or to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (take the 100E airport bus for ~900 HUF from Deák Ferenc tér).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Budapest. Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most historically rich and beautiful cities.

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian breakfast – try a full breakfast at a local café: eggs, cold cuts, fresh bread, and coffee for ~1,500–2,000 HUF
meals.lunch: Quick and budget-friendly farewell meal – lángos or a kebab near the market for ~1,000–1,500 HUF
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal, or grab a sandwich from a supermarket before departure

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate: Prague (Days 1–4) ~$30–45/day including accommodation, food, transport, and entry fees. Budapest (Days 5–8) ~$35–50/day. Total 8-day trip budget estimate: $280–$380 USD excluding flights. Always carry some local cash as smaller establishments may not accept cards. September is an ideal time to visit – mild weather, fewer crowds than summer, and no major price surges.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Václav Havel Airport Prague at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Airport Express bus or taxi to your accommodation in central Prague. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite near the hotel if hungry — try a local kebab shop or a 24-hour convenience store snack to tide you over until morning.

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives late, so Day 1 is purely a travel and check-in day. Keep it stress-free. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid delays. Prague's city center is approximately 30–40 minutes from the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Start your Prague exploration with a leisurely walk through the Old Town (Staré Město). Visit the iconic Old Town Square, admire the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and watch the hourly show, and explore the Gothic Týn Church. Stroll through the winding medieval streets and soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the magnificent Charles Bridge (Karlův most), pausing to enjoy the views of the Vltava River and the statues lining the bridge. Continue into Malá Strana (Lesser Town) and climb up to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Allow 2–3 hours for the castle complex.
day_by_day.evening: Descend back into the city center and enjoy a relaxed evening stroll along the riverbank. Head to the Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhood for dinner at a traditional Czech restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre or a local bakery near your hotel — try a croissant or traditional Czech pastry with coffee (budget: ~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Café Savoy in Malá Strana — classic Czech cuisine in a beautiful Art Nouveau setting, mid-range pricing (~€12–18)
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá — a beloved Prague pub-restaurant serving authentic Czech dishes like svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) and freshly tapped Pilsner Urquell (~€15–22)

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is best visited in the morning or afternoon on weekdays to avoid peak crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the castle district involves a steep uphill walk. The Astronomical Clock show happens every hour on the hour.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — one of Europe's best-preserved Jewish heritage sites. Explore the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Pinkas Synagogue (a Holocaust memorial), and the Spanish Synagogue with its stunning Moorish interior. Purchase a combined ticket for access to multiple synagogues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Wenceslas Square area and visit the National Museum (Národní muzeum) — recently renovated and showcasing Czech history and natural history. Afterward, explore the nearby Lucerna Passage, a beautiful Art Nouveau arcade with quirky art installations.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Prague's vibrant cultural scene — attend a classical music concert or Mozart opera performance at one of Prague's historic venues (Estates Theatre or Municipal House). Book tickets in advance online.

meals.breakfast: Eska Bakery — a trendy Prague bakery with excellent sourdough breads, pastries, and specialty coffee (~€6–9)
meals.lunch: Nase Maso — a popular butcher-restaurant in the Jewish Quarter area offering excellent Czech meat dishes and sandwiches (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner at Café Imperial — a stunning Art Nouveau café near Municipal House, serving Czech and European cuisine (~€18–25)

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter combined ticket costs approximately €25–30 and covers most synagogues and the cemetery. Book concert tickets at least 1–2 days in advance, especially in September when the tourist season is still active. The Estates Theatre is where Mozart himself premiered Don Giovanni in 1787.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to Vyšehrad — Prague's lesser-known but equally historic fortress overlooking the Vltava River. Explore the neo-Gothic Basilica of St. Peter and St. Paul, the ancient Rotunda of St. Martin, and the famous Vyšehrad Cemetery where Czech luminaries like Antonín Dvořák are buried. Enjoy panoramic views of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit the Prague City Museum (Muzeum hlavního města Prahy) for a deeper dive into Prague's urban history, including the famous Langweil model of 19th-century Prague. Afterward, explore the trendy Vinohrady neighborhood with its beautiful Art Nouveau apartment buildings and boutique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Pack your bags and prepare for your early morning departure to Budapest. Explore the lively bar scene in Žižkov or Vinohrady for a farewell Prague evening — try a traditional Czech pivnice (pub) for one last local beer.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café in your accommodation area (~€6–10)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch at Vyšehrad Park — grab supplies from a local Billa or Albert supermarket (great mid-range option, ~€6–8)
meals.dinner: Hospůdka Na Hradbách — a cozy restaurant right inside the Vyšehrad complex with Czech comfort food and river views (~€14–20)

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is far less crowded than Prague Castle and offers a more authentic, peaceful experience. September weather in Prague averages 15–20°C — bring a light jacket for evenings. Begin packing tonight as you'll travel to Budapest tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the morning RegioJet or FlixBus from Prague to Budapest (approximately 7 hours, depart ~08:00, arrive ~15:00) — book in advance for best mid-range prices (~€20–35). Alternatively, take a train via Vienna. Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest and check in to your accommodation. Once settled, take a gentle orientation walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side, admiring the spectacular views of Buda Castle and the Chain Bridge. Stroll to the iconic Hungarian Parliament Building for exterior photos.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Budapest with a relaxing visit to one of the city's famous thermal bath spas — Széchenyi Baths (open until 22:00) is a magnificent Neo-Baroque complex perfect for unwinding after a travel day.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Prague's Florenc bus/train station or grab snacks for the journey (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: On-board snacks or stop at a service area during the bus journey (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Borkonyha Winekitchen near the Parliament — a Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant offering modern Hungarian cuisine at reasonable mid-range prices (~€18–28)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague–Budapest transport at least 3–5 days in advance, especially for weekend travel. RegioJet offers comfortable coaches with Wi-Fi and onboard service. Széchenyi Baths entry costs approximately €20–25 including locker rental. Bring a towel or rent one on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Buda side of the city — take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) up Castle Hill. Visit Buda Castle (Budavári Palota) and the Hungarian National Gallery inside. Wander through the charming Castle District streets, visit the Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) with its stunning geometric tiled roof, and admire the Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) for breathtaking panoramic views of the Danube and Pest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Castle Hill and cross the iconic Széchenyi Chain Bridge on foot. Explore the vibrant Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) — Budapest's largest and most spectacular indoor market — browse stalls selling Hungarian paprika, salami, embroidery, and local produce.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter and the famous Ruin Bars (romkocsmák) — Budapest's unique bar culture set in abandoned buildings. Visit Szimpla Kert, the original and most iconic ruin bar, for drinks in an eclectic, artistic atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square — a legendary Budapest coffeehouse serving pastries, cakes, and coffee since 1858 (~€8–12)
meals.lunch: Grab a langos (fried dough with toppings) or kürtőskalács (chimney cake) at the Great Market Hall food stalls — an authentic and affordable local experience (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: Kárpátia Restaurant near the Inner City — a historic Budapest restaurant in a stunning Neo-Gothic hall serving traditional Hungarian goulash, pörkölt, and paprikás csirke (~€16–24)

day_by_day.notes: Fisherman's Bastion is free to visit the outer terraces; there's a small fee for the upper towers. Sunday is a great day to visit the Great Market Hall as it has reduced hours (open until 15:00), so plan accordingly. Ruin bars typically get lively after 21:00.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of the most stunning Neo-Gothic buildings in the world and the largest building in Hungary. Book a guided interior tour in advance (approximately €15–20) to see the Crown Jewels and ornate ceremonial halls. Afterward, walk to St. Stephen's Basilica (Szent István-bazilika) and climb to the dome for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's grand UNESCO-listed boulevard lined with Neo-Renaissance mansions, embassies, and boutiques. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House for a guided tour or check for evening performance tickets. Continue to Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the adjacent City Park (Városliget), home to Vajdahunyad Castle.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a Danube River cruise at sunset — several operators offer 1–2 hour evening cruises with stunning illuminated views of both banks of the Danube, including Parliament, Buda Castle, and the Chain Bridge. Book in advance (~€15–25).

meals.breakfast: Auguszt Cukrászda — a beloved family-run Budapest pastry shop serving traditional Hungarian rétes (strudel) and cakes (~€6–9)
meals.lunch: Menza Restaurant on Liszt Ferenc Square — a stylish bistro with a retro-Socialist design serving modern Hungarian classics at mid-range prices (~€12–18)
meals.dinner: Onboard light snacks during the Danube cruise, followed by dinner at Costes Downtown — a refined but accessible modern European restaurant near the waterfront (~€22–32)

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online in advance at the official website — slots fill up quickly, especially on weekends. The Danube cruise is most magical at dusk when the city lights begin to illuminate. Andrássy Avenue is also home to the Terror House Museum (House of Terror) if you're interested in 20th-century Hungarian history.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit the Dohány Street Synagogue (Nagy Zsinagóga), the largest synagogue in Europe and a powerful symbol of Budapest's Jewish heritage. Explore the adjacent Jewish Museum and the moving Holocaust Memorial in the garden. Afterward, browse the antique shops and bookstores along Falk Miksa Street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Váci Street pedestrian zone or the Design Terminal market. Visit the Hungarian Museum of Fine Arts at Heroes' Square if time permits. Begin making your way to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for your departure, allowing at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Budapest — reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most magnificent cities.

meals.breakfast: New York Café — a legendary, ornately decorated Budapest coffeehouse often called 'the most beautiful café in the world' — a perfect farewell breakfast (~€12–18)
meals.lunch: Fröccsterasz near the Danube — a casual Hungarian wine bar and restaurant serving light bites, Hungarian wines, and fröccs (wine spritzer) (~€10–15)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner near your hotel before heading to the airport (~€12–18)

day_by_day.notes: The Dohány Street Synagogue requires modest dress (shoulders and knees covered) — scarves are available at the entrance. Budapest Airport is approximately 30–40 minutes from the city center by taxi or the 100E airport bus. Allow extra time for Monday–Tuesday morning traffic. Keep some Hungarian Forints (HUF) for last-minute purchases as not all smaller vendors accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrival at Prague Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to your hotel in the heart of Prague. Check-in, unwind with a welcome drink at the hotel bar, and settle into your premium accommodations. Light room service recommended after a long journey.

meals.breakfast: On board or at departure airport
meals.lunch: On board or at departure airport
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining or hotel bar — order a charcuterie board, Czech open-faced sandwiches (chlebíčky), and a glass of Moravian wine to ease into the destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with hotel. Keep Day 1 light — rest is essential for the days ahead. Prague is in Central European Time (CET, UTC+1).

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the hotel. Begin your Prague immersion with a private guided walking tour of the UNESCO-listed Prague Old Town (Staré Město). Explore the astronomical clock (Orloj) at Old Town Square, the Gothic Church of Our Lady before Týn, and the medieval lanes of Josefov (the historic Jewish Quarter). Visit the Old Jewish Cemetery — one of the most haunting and historically significant sites in Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Charles Bridge (Karlův Most) adorned with Baroque statues, then ascend to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Tour St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička). Enjoy panoramic views over the red-roofed city from the castle ramparts. Private guide included throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) with its Baroque palaces and cobblestone streets. Dinner at a top-tier Prague restaurant — book a table at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise (Michelin-starred) for an extraordinary tasting menu rooted in historic Czech cuisine with modern luxury execution.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate hotel breakfast buffet or à la carte — fresh pastries, smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, fresh juices
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Café Savoy in Malá Strana — Art Nouveau interiors, refined Czech cuisine, duck confit, and house-baked sourdough
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — 11-course tasting menu with wine pairing (Michelin-starred). Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle opens at 09:00. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestones. Private guide recommended for historical depth. September weather is mild (14–20°C) — bring a light layer for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the magnificent Lobkowicz Palace inside Prague Castle complex — a privately owned palace with original Beethoven manuscripts, Bruegel paintings, and remarkable Habsburg collections. Then explore the Strahov Monastery Library, one of the most beautiful Baroque libraries in the world, with its Theological and Philosophical Halls filled with centuries-old manuscripts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Discover the Mucha Museum dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alphonse Mucha, followed by a private visit to the Museum of Decorative Arts. Afternoon at leisure to explore Vinohrady neighborhood — Prague's elegant residential district with Art Nouveau architecture, boutique shops, and café culture. Consider a stop at the historic Lucerna Palace arcade.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music performance — Prague is renowned for its concert culture. Book tickets for a performance at the Rudolfinum (home of the Czech Philharmonic) or the stunning Estates Theatre (where Mozart himself conducted Don Giovanni in 1787). Pre-concert dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — freshly baked croissants, artisan cheeses, cold cuts, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Eska Restaurant — award-winning farm-to-table Czech cuisine in a beautifully converted industrial space; sourdough bread, heritage grain dishes, seasonal vegetables
meals.dinner: Field Restaurant — contemporary Czech fine dining with a focus on local, seasonal ingredients; pre-concert timing recommended. Three-course menu with sommelier-selected wines.

day_by_day.notes: Book concert tickets well in advance — Estates Theatre and Rudolfinum sell out quickly, especially in September. Lobkowicz Palace requires separate entry from the main castle ticket.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure for spa treatment at the hotel or a final Prague exploration. Visit the Veletržní Palace (Trade Fair Palace) — home to the National Gallery's impressive collection of modern and contemporary art including works by Picasso, Klimt, and Czech masters. Alternatively, explore the vibrant Náplavka riverside farmers market (weekends) or stroll along the Vltava embankment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Prague to Budapest by premium car service or first-class rail (approximately 6–7 hours scenic journey through Central European countryside — consider the scenic Railjet train for an experience). Alternatively, a short 1-hour flight can be arranged for maximum efficiency. Arrive Budapest and check into your luxury accommodations in the heart of the city.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Budapest — take a relaxed orientation stroll along the Danube promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side. Admire the illuminated Hungarian Parliament Building (one of Europe's most spectacular Gothic Revival structures) and the Chain Bridge glowing at night. Welcome dinner at a prestigious Budapest restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Final Prague hotel breakfast — indulge fully before the journey
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic prepared by the hotel for the journey, or dining car on the train, or airport lounge if flying
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown (Budapest, Michelin-starred) — Hungarian-inspired contemporary cuisine with an exceptional wine list featuring Tokaj and Eger wines. Perfect introduction to Budapest's gastronomic scene.

day_by_day.notes: If traveling by train, book first-class Railjet seats on the Prague–Budapest route. Journey time is approximately 6h 45min with beautiful countryside scenery. Private car transfer is also available (~5.5 hours). Confirm Budapest hotel late afternoon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with a private guided tour of Buda Castle District (Castle Hill) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore Matthias Church with its stunning Zsolnay tile roof, the Fisherman's Bastion offering breathtaking panoramic views over the Danube and Pest skyline, and the Royal Palace complex housing the Hungarian National Gallery. Walk the medieval lanes of the Castle District.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the city and cross the legendary Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot. Explore the elegant Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's Champs-Élysées — a UNESCO-listed boulevard lined with Neo-Renaissance palaces, luxury boutiques, and embassies. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House for a guided interior tour (one of Europe's most opulent opera houses). Explore the upscale Váci Street and Vörösmarty Square area.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House — book premium seats for an unforgettable evening of opera or ballet in one of the world's most beautiful opera interiors. Alternatively, enjoy a Danube dinner cruise on a luxury private boat with live music, champagne, and panoramic views of the illuminated city.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Hungarian specialties including lángos (fried dough), túrós táska (cottage cheese pastry), fresh fruit, and strong espresso
meals.lunch: Borkonyha (Wine Kitchen, Michelin-starred) — sophisticated Hungarian cuisine with an extraordinary wine selection; located steps from the Basilica
meals.dinner: Pre-opera dinner at Onyx Restaurant (Michelin-starred, located on Vörösmarty Square) — Hungary's pinnacle of fine dining with avant-garde Hungarian cuisine and impeccable service

day_by_day.notes: Opera House tickets should be booked weeks in advance. Fisherman's Bastion is best visited early morning to avoid crowds. September evenings in Budapest are beautiful — around 15–18°C, perfect for evening strolls.

day_by_day.morning: Experience Budapest's legendary thermal bath culture — visit Széchenyi Thermal Bath (the largest medicinal bath in Europe, housed in a stunning Neo-Baroque palace) or the more intimate and architecturally extraordinary Gellért Thermal Bath for a VIP private session. Enjoy the mineral-rich thermal pools, steam rooms, and massage treatments in a truly historic setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) — Budapest's magnificent iron-and-glass covered market — for artisan Hungarian products, paprika, Tokaj wine, and handcrafts. Then visit the remarkable Dohány Street Synagogue — the largest synagogue in Europe and second largest in the world — with its moving Holocaust memorial garden and Jewish Museum. Explore the vibrant Jewish Quarter (Erzsébetváros) and its famous ruin bars.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset visit to Gellért Hill and the Citadella for the most spectacular panoramic view of Budapest and the Danube at golden hour. Dinner at a rooftop restaurant with city views, followed by cocktails at one of Budapest's legendary rooftop bars.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast before the thermal bath experience
meals.lunch: Stand25 Bistro — celebrated Budapest bistro known for exceptional Hungarian classics including gulyás, töltött káposzta (stuffed cabbage), and house-made pálinka
meals.dinner: Babel Budapest (Michelin-starred) — innovative Hungarian fine dining that reinterprets traditional flavors with modern techniques; exceptional tasting menu with Hungarian wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book VIP thermal bath session in advance — private cabins and massage treatments fill up quickly. Gellért Hill sunset is approximately 19:00–19:30 in mid-September. The Jewish Quarter comes alive in the evening — worth a post-dinner exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or extended exploration to the Buda Hills and surrounding areas. Visit the extraordinary Memento Park — an open-air museum housing giant Communist-era statues removed after 1989, offering a unique insight into Hungary's 20th-century history. Alternatively, explore the elegant suburb of Óbuda (Old Buda) with its Roman ruins at Aquincum — the former Roman legionary town and capital of Pannonia Inferior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Budapest for a private guided tour of the Hungarian Parliament Building — one of the world's most beautiful legislative buildings, featuring the Holy Crown of St. Stephen and extraordinary Neo-Gothic interiors. Then explore Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Museum of Fine Arts with its world-class collection of European masterworks (El Greco, Raphael, Rembrandt, Monet).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Budapest dinner — experience the pinnacle of Hungarian hospitality. Book a private dining experience or chef's table at one of Budapest's elite restaurants. After dinner, enjoy a nightcap at the rooftop bar of a luxury hotel overlooking the illuminated Parliament and Danube — a memory to last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast at the hotel — a celebratory start to your penultimate full day
meals.lunch: Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most historic and iconic café (est. 1858); enjoy Dobos torte, Esterházy cake, and fine coffee in grand imperial surroundings
meals.dinner: Tanti Restaurant or Asador Restaurant — exceptional Hungarian fine dining with seasonal tasting menus; alternatively, a private chef's table experience arranged through your hotel concierge

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked in advance — English-language guided tours available. Memento Park is approximately 30 minutes from the city center by private car. Consider a sunset Danube cruise as an alternative evening activity.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — enjoy a leisurely luxury hotel breakfast. Last-minute exploration of the elegant Belváros (Inner City) district, the romantic Elizabeth Bridge area, or a final coffee at a historic Budapest café. Visit the Central Kavéház (Central Café) — one of Budapest's grandest coffee houses, restored to its original 1887 splendor, for a farewell espresso and pastry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of hotel. Private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport. Departure lounge access recommended — use the SkyCourt or airline lounge for a comfortable pre-flight experience. Reflect on an extraordinary 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most magnificent capitals.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry home memories of golden Prague spires, Budapest's thermal waters, Michelin-starred meals, world-class music, and the rich tapestry of Central European history and culture.

meals.breakfast: Grand final hotel breakfast — order everything you haven't tried yet: Hungarian pastries, cold cuts, fresh juices, specialty eggs
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport lounge or a quick stop at a café near the hotel before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in. Budapest airport is approximately 30–40 minutes from the city center. Arrange private transfer through your hotel concierge. Duty-free shopping available for Tokaj wine, Hungarian pálinka, and Zsolnay porcelain as premium souvenirs.
